title: First Sunday of Advent (Mark 13:33–37)
hookLine: the new year starts with watch

lines: THE FIRST WORD IS A COMMAND.
cards: New Year's Eve has a countdown and a party. The Church's new year begins on a Sunday in late November or early December, in purple, with a single candle and a warning. No fireworks.
The first gospel of the year isn't a birth story. It's a house at night, a master who has gone away, and a doorkeeper told to stay awake.
In the year when Mark's Gospel is read on Sundays, these five verses, Mark 13:33 to 37, open everything. And the year's first word is a command.

teach.b: Advent comes from the Latin adventus, a coming or an arrival.

Across the Sundays before Christmas, the Church looks two ways at once: back to the first coming, the birth in Bethlehem, and forward to the coming at the end of time. The first Sunday leans hard forward.
In Mark, Jesus tells a small story.
A man goes on a long journey. He leaves his house in his servants' hands, gives each one a job, and tells the porter at the door to keep watch.
Nobody knows when he'll be back: in the evening, at midnight, at cockcrow, or in the morning.
Four times, named one after another, so every hour of the dark is covered. Don't let him come suddenly and find you sleeping.

Then the last line, which Mark aims past the disciples at every reader: "And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch." The Greek word is grēgoreite, stay awake, keep alert, a word for staying up when sleep would be easier.
Notice what it doesn't say: panic, or calculate the date, or stare at the sky. Each servant has work.
Watching, in this story, looks like doing your job well while staying awake to who might walk through the door.

teach.h: WHAT I SAY TO YOU, I SAY TO ALL: WATCH.
teach.b: That's why the Church starts its year here. Before the manger, before the shepherds and the star, the first thing asked is attention.
And on this Sunday, in some homes, someone lights the first of four candles on a wreath: one small flame against the dark.

how: On the First Sunday of Advent, Catholic churches begin the new liturgical year in violet vestments, and many parishes and families light the first candle of an Advent wreath.

o: Greek: be still and wait quietly

games.why: keep watch. he might come at evening, midnight, cockcrow or morning, and he must not find you sleeping.

practice: If you have an Advent wreath, light the first candle; if not, any candle, or a single lamp in a dark room, will do.

Watch the flame the way a doorkeeper watches a door, awake, unhurried, ready, and when your mind wanders, come back to the light. If you pray, you can say the word Advent keeps singing, come; if not, just keep watch with the flame.
